title: paged KV cache: block allocator reuse, pinning, and TTL optimizations
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: reduce tail latency and memory churn in the paged KV cache by reusing block allocator state, avoiding redundant allocations on pin/unpin, and introducing a configurable TTL for pinned blocks to bound memory held by long-lived sessions. This PR makes three related changes in the paged KV cache block manager: 1) allocator reuse: the block allocator now keeps a small pool of recently freed blocks keyed by size class to avoid repeated expensive allocations and device memory map churn; 2) lightweight pinning: pin/unpin operations are now O(1) and avoid moving blocks when possible by using a generation tag to detect staleness rather than immediate copies; 3) pinned-block TTL: pinned blocks can be annotated with an optional TTL so long-lived sequences do not indefinitely prevent reuse. Summary of changes, rationale, and risk mitigations are in the commit messages. Performance: internal bench harness shows 12-18% p99 latency reduction for steady-state streaming workloads with long context reuse, and 7-10% reduction in per-token GPU memory overhead on 32GB A100 instance profiles. Compatibility: behavior is backwards-compatible by default; allocator reuse and TTL are configurable via runtime flags and default to conservative settings. Rollout plan: feature gated via runtime config, staged rollout to canary followed by region-by-region ramp with metrics: p99 latency, allocator miss rate, memory-reserved. Testing: unit tests for allocator pool invariants, integration tests exercising pin/unpin and TTL expiry, stress test with continuous batching harness. Checklist: [x] design doc linked in ENG-2021, [x] unit tests, [x] perf benchmarks, [x] docs update in redwood-docs (pending small doc patch), [x] feature flag. Breaking change: none by default.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice work. Two concerns: the allocator pool size default seems conservative, can we justify with perf data? Also please add an assertion in debug builds to catch double-unpin races.

Maya Patel: replied: added microbench numbers to the PR description and increased debug assertions behind cfg(debug_assertions). Kept default pool small (4 per size class) to avoid increased resident set for small configs; we can tune post-rollout.
Ravi Desai: requested changes: make TTL configurable per-tenant and ensure expiry sweep runs off critical path. Also add tracing spans for pin/unpin to help SLO debugging.

Maya Patel: replied: made TTL configurable via runtime tenant config, moved expiry sweep to background worker with bounded budget, and added tracing spans. Pushed tests and a perf run with new defaults.
Anya Sokolov: approved after validation on canary; observed no regression on small-context workloads and p99 improved on long-context tests.
